nodes.label: FP: Pure Function principle
nodes.rationale: A function is pure if, given the same inputs, it always returns the same output and has no side effects (no mutation of external state, no I/O, no globals). Pure functions are trivially testable — no mocks needed, just input to output.

nodes.label: FP: Immutability principle
nodes.rationale: Never mutate a struct passed as a parameter; always return a new copy with the changes applied. This prevents a whole class of bugs where shared state is modified unexpectedly across function boundaries.

nodes.label: FP: No Side Effects / separation of computation from I/O
nodes.rationale: Side effects (DB writes, HTTP calls, logging) belong in the handler or repository layer, never inside a service function that computes a result. Separating computation from I/O makes each piece independently testable.
nodes.norm_label: fp: no side effects / separation of computation from i/o

nodes.label: CORS hand-written over rs/cors library
nodes.rationale: Writing CORS manually (~20 lines) is consistent with the net/http-stdlib-only philosophy and serves as a learning exercise; rs/cors would be adopted if edge cases like multiple origins or credential headers become important.

nodes.label: DBPinger interface over *sql.DB directly
nodes.rationale: DatabaseChecker accepts a narrow DBPinger interface (one method, PingContext) instead of *sql.DB, letting tests inject a mock without a real database connection; *sql.DB satisfies DBPinger implicitly in production.

nodes.label: BuildHandler extracted from main()
nodes.rationale: main() calls os.Exit and blocks on a channel, making it untestable directly; extracting BuildHandler(cfg, registry) into server.go gives tests a clean entry point with a real registry and mock checkers, no OS signals, no real DB.

nodes.label: Auth Feature (login, refresh-token, logout, unlock, JWT middleware, rate limiting)
nodes.norm_label: auth feature (login, refresh-token, logout, unlock, jwt middleware, rate limiting)

nodes.label: Stateful JWT via JTI column
nodes.rationale: Each access token carries a jti (UUID v4) claim; the server stores only the jti (not the full token) in users.access_token_jti. RequireAuth verifies the JWT signature locally then checks jti against the DB value for revocation, avoiding full-token storage.

nodes.label: Refresh token format {userID}.{randomHex}
nodes.rationale: Semi-opaque format embeds the user ID to avoid a full-table hash lookup on refresh while a 64-byte random hex provides 256 bits of entropy; a deliberate deviation from a fully-opaque token, which would have made reuse detection (clearing DB tokens on reuse) impossible without knowing the user ID.

nodes.label: CORS default changed from * to http://localhost:3000
nodes.rationale: HTTP-only cookies cannot be set cross-origin when Allow-Origin is '*', because browsers disallow combining a wildcard origin with Allow-Credentials: true.
nodes.norm_label: cors default changed from * to http://localhost:3000

nodes.label: In-memory token bucket rate limiter
nodes.rationale: golang.org/x/time/rate token bucket (10 req/min/IP) is acceptable at current scale even though counters reset on restart; a Redis-backed limiter would be needed for multi-instance deployments.

nodes.label: Account lockout after 5 failed login attempts

nodes.label: Event Submission Feature (public, contributor lookup/creation, slug reuse)
nodes.norm_label: event submission feature (public, contributor lookup/creation, slug reuse)

nodes.label: Partial unique index for slug reuse
nodes.rationale: events_slug_idx is UNIQUE(slug) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND status IN ('pending','approved'), letting a rejected event keep its slug in the row for history while allowing a new submission to reuse that slug — enforced at the DB level, not just in application code.
nodes.norm_label: partial unique index for slug reuse

nodes.label: AuditLog construction stays in repository, not service
nodes.rationale: The service layer is pure and cannot know post-insert IDs; buildSubmissionAuditLogs is a plain, non-FP helper that lives in the repository and runs after tx.Create(&event) inside the same transaction, keeping the service free of I/O.
nodes.norm_label: auditlog construction stays in repository, not service

nodes.label: Contributor lookup/creation/rename on submission
nodes.rationale: findOrCreateSubmitter overwrites an existing user's name with the new submitter name but preserves their existing role, preventing a public submission from ever escalating or downgrading an account's role.

nodes.label: FP-annotated service layer for event submission (ValidateSubmitEventInput, BuildEventFromInput, BuildDeadlinesFromInput, BuildSubmitterFromInput, BuildSubmission)

nodes.label: Events List Feature (filterable, paginated, bbox, tier, first_deadline_month)
nodes.norm_label: events list feature (filterable, paginated, bbox, tier, first_deadline_month)

nodes.label: Pagination defaults must always be present
nodes.rationale: GORM's Limit(0) returns zero rows, not 'no limit', so Page/PageSize must always be populated (1/20 default) even for pagination=off calls; PaginationOff is the actual switch that skips Limit/Offset.
nodes.norm_label: pagination defaults must always be present

nodes.label: first_deadline_month via correlated EXISTS+MIN subquery
nodes.rationale: Filtering events by their earliest active abstract/paper deadline's month and year is implemented as a single correlated subquery rather than a join, keeping the count query and select query symmetric.

nodes.label: GORM zero-value bool + gorm:default tag gotcha
nodes.rationale: Deadline{IsActive:false} on Create is silently converted to the column default (true) by GORM; inactive test data must be created active then updated via tx.Model().Update(), which mirrors exactly how the application supersedes deadlines in production.
nodes.norm_label: gorm zero-value bool + gorm:default tag gotcha

nodes.label: Admin/Moderator Event Review feature (approve/reject, partial edit, reviewer reason)
nodes.norm_label: admin/moderator event review feature (approve/reject, partial edit, reviewer reason)

nodes.label: GORM Omit(clause.Associations) fix
nodes.rationale: A plain tx.Save() on an event that still carries stale CreatedBy/LastUpdatedBy associations from an earlier reload overwrites the explicitly-set LastUpdatedByID foreign key; Omit(clause.Associations) stops GORM from re-saving those associations.

nodes.label: Shared parseDateField helper
nodes.rationale: Submit and Review handlers both needed identical YYYY-MM-DD parsing and error messages; extracting parseDateField gives one place to change the date format and guarantees identical error text across endpoints.

nodes.label: Reusing ValidateEditedEvent for partial updates
nodes.rationale: Merging optional review edits onto the existing event and validating with the exact same per-field checks as submission guarantees a reviewer's edit can never produce an event that wouldn't have passed original submission validation.

nodes.label: date stays separate; time/timezone are independent nullable additions
nodes.rationale: Rather than combining into a single timestamptz, time and timezone are plain nullable columns, keeping existing date-based queries (first_deadline_month, sorting) unchanged while allowing date-only, date+time, or date+time+timezone deadlines.

nodes.label: One audit row per logical change, not per row written
nodes.rationale: Adding N deadlines writes exactly 2 audit rows total: one deadline_added/batch_deadlines_added row and one always-written updated row for the last_updated_by_id change, establishing the pattern for all future event-update endpoints.
nodes.norm_label: one audit row per logical change, not per row written

nodes.label: No automatic supersession (documented limitation)
nodes.rationale: There is no reliable signal to distinguish an update to an existing deadline from a genuinely new deadline with a similar description, so duplicate deadlines are accepted as new active rows until a dedicated supersession endpoint exists.

nodes.label: Cancelled vs superseded share is_active=false, distinguished by superseded_by_id
nodes.rationale: Cancelling never sets superseded_by_id, leaving it NULL to mean 'no replacement'; ValidateDeadlineCancellable treats both cancelled and superseded as DEADLINE_ALREADY_INACTIVE since the cancel endpoint has no need to distinguish them.
nodes.norm_label: cancelled vs superseded share is_active=false, distinguished by superseded_by_id

nodes.label: validateSubmitterInput extracted as shared pure function
nodes.rationale: All three endpoints accepting a submitter:{name,email} body now share one validation function in internal/service/event.go, removing triplicated inline checks.
nodes.norm_label: validatesubmitterinput extracted as shared pure function

nodes.label: Supersede a Deadline feature (replace active deadline, immutable history chain)
nodes.norm_label: supersede a deadline feature (replace active deadline, immutable history chain)

nodes.label: Time/timezone one-way data flow from request, never from old row
nodes.rationale: BuildSupersedingDeadline reads Date/Time/Timezone only from the input, never from the old deadline, structurally enforcing the 'never inherit time/timezone' spec rule since there is no code path for old values to leak through.
nodes.norm_label: time/timezone one-way data flow from request, never from old row

nodes.label: preloadEventAssociations widened to include superseded rows
nodes.rationale: Changing the Deadlines preload condition to is_active=true OR superseded_by_id IS NOT NULL made every reload endpoint (list, add, cancel, supersede) return superseded deadlines alongside active ones with a single shared-helper change.
nodes.norm_label: preloadeventassociations widened to include superseded rows

nodes.label: OpenTelemetry Tracing feature (HTTP + DB spans exported to Sentry via sentryotel)
nodes.norm_label: opentelemetry tracing feature (http + db spans exported to sentry via sentryotel)

nodes.label: sentryotel bridge chosen over manual OTLP exporter
nodes.rationale: The original spec drafted a manually-derived Sentry OTLP endpoint with an x-sentry-auth header; research confirmed the Sentry-documented path is sentry.Init + sentryotel.NewSentrySpanProcessor + sentryotel.NewSentryPropagator, avoiding a brittle, unsupported integration.
nodes.norm_label: sentryotel bridge chosen over manual otlp exporter

nodes.label: ParentBased(TraceIDRatioBased) sampling, rate 1.0 dev / 0.2 prod
nodes.rationale: Full sampling in development aids debugging while 20% sampling in production limits volume/cost; the OTel sampler is meant to be the single source of truth for which spans are created, never 0.

nodes.label: API Client + Error Handling feature (typed fetch client, error-to-toast mapping)
nodes.norm_label: api client + error handling feature (typed fetch client, error-to-toast mapping)

nodes.label: shadcn/ui manual setup instead of CLI
nodes.rationale: Neither shadcn CLI version (2.3.0, 4.11) worked: v4.11's new preset registry 404s and doesn't map to 'Neutral', v2.3.0 doesn't support Tailwind v4's CSS-first config, so the equivalent setup was built by hand following shadcn's documented Tailwind v4 conventions.
nodes.norm_label: shadcn/ui manual setup instead of cli

nodes.label: Hand-written src/types/api.ts as temporary exception
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md bans hand-writing API types in favor of OpenAPI-generated types, but no OpenAPI spec exists yet, so types were transcribed from the backend YAML specs as a deliberate, temporary exception.

nodes.label: eslint downgraded from ^10 to ^9
nodes.rationale: eslint-plugin-react (pulled in by eslint-config-next) calls the removed context.getFilename() API and crashes under ESLint 10; eslint-config-next's own peerDependencies require eslint >=9.0.0, so v9 is the actually-supported version, not a regression.

nodes.label: Session: OpenTelemetry Tracing — Sentry Double-Sampling Bug Fix
nodes.norm_label: session: opentelemetry tracing — sentry double-sampling bug fix

nodes.label: Sentry double-sampling bug: unset TracesSampleRate silently drops all transactions
nodes.rationale: sentry.Init was called with EnableTracing:true but TracesSampleRate defaulted to 0.0; the sentryotel span processor's fallback sampling decision then rejected every transaction independently of the OTel ParentBased sampler, stacking two independent sampling gates where the second always rejected everything. Fixed by setting TracesSampleRate:1.0 so OTel remains the single source of truth for which spans are created.
nodes.norm_label: sentry double-sampling bug: unset tracessamplerate silently drops all transactions

nodes.label: useTranslations() reference stored in useRef to fix re-fetch loop
nodes.rationale: useTranslations() returns a new function reference every render; placing it directly in a useEffect dependency array caused a re-fetch after every state update, fixed by storing it in a ref and reading tRef.current inside the effect.

nodes.label: Validation errors stored in useRef, not useState
nodes.rationale: validateStep2() is called synchronously and the caller checks the errors object immediately after; useState would require a re-render cycle before the updated value is visible, so errorsRef.current is mutated in place with a dummy state bump to trigger the UI re-render while keeping synchronous reads correct.
nodes.norm_label: validation errors stored in useref, not usestate

nodes.label: cancelled flag fixes Leaflet StrictMode double-init
nodes.rationale: In React StrictMode the cleanup function runs before the async import('leaflet') promise resolves, so the DOM container stays registered and a second mount's L.map(container) throws 'Map container is already initialized'; a cancelled boolean checked inside the .then() callback prevents the second init.
nodes.norm_label: cancelled flag fixes leaflet strictmode double-init
